gaps.sentence: There's ___ point asking him again — he never replies.
gaps.explanation: 'There's no point' — 'point' needs the adjective 'no', not the pronoun 'none'.
'Cut something in half' is the fixed expression; 'in middle' would need 'the middle'.

gaps.sentence: The village is remote and has ___ facilities — not even a post office.
gaps.hint: negative meaning with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Few facilities' means almost none, which matches 'not even a post office'; 'facilities' is countable.

gaps.hint: price per item comes at the end
gaps.explanation: 'Fifteen pounds each' means fifteen pounds per ticket; 'every' cannot stand alone in this position.

gaps.sentence: She has two children. One lives in Leeds, and ___ lives in York.
gaps.hint: one of a pair of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... the other ...' is the pattern for exactly two; 'another' would imply more than two.

gaps.sentence: ___ lakes in this region freeze in winter.
gaps.explanation: 'Most lakes' speaks about lakes in general; 'most of' would need 'the lakes'.

gaps.sentence: I haven't got ___ cash on me — I'll pay by card.
gaps.explanation: 'Any' is the normal quantifier in negative sentences; 'haven't got no cash' would be a double negative.
'Several charges' means more than two; the other options are used only with uncountable nouns.
